questions.prompt: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Only plant cells have a cell wall. Both kinds of cell have a membrane and a nucleus.

questions.prompt: What substance is the plant cell wall made of?
questions.explanation: The cell wall is made of cellulose. Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: What takes place in the chloroplasts?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis. Respiration takes place in the mitochondria.

questions.prompt: A cell has a nucleus, a cell membrane, small vacuoles and no cell wall. It is most likely...
questions.explanation: No cell wall and only small vacuoles are features of animal cells. Plant cells, including leaf cells, have a cell wall.

questions.prompt: Why do plant cells have a fixed, regular shape?
options: They have a rigid cell wall
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall holds the shape. Animal cells also have a nucleus and mitochondria, and their shapes vary.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true of both plant cells and animal cells?
options: Both have a cell membrane and mitochondria
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts and cell walls are found only in plant cells. The membrane and mitochondria are in both.

questions.prompt: Which green pigment is found in chloroplasts?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment used in photosynthesis. Cell sap is the liquid in the vacuole.
